d.d: (engineering, euphemistic) Synonym of rapid unplanned disassembly: An unexpected explosion or breakup.
Any species of the freshwater game fishes of genus Scardinius.
An underwater vane used to steer a vessel. The rudder is controlled by means of a wheel, tiller or other apparatus (modern vessels can be controlled even with a joystick or an autopilot).

A control surface on the vertical stabilizer of a fixed-wing aircraft or an autogyro. On some craft, the entire vertical stabilizer comprises the rudder. The rudder is controlled by foot-operated control pedals.
Reddish in color, especially of the face, fire, or sky.
Robust and vigorous, like a person with a red complexion (as compared to a pale one).
Lacking in refinement or civility; bad-mannered; discourteous.
d.x: This girl was so rude towards the cashier by screaming at him for no apparent reason.

d.d: Lacking refinement or skill; untaught; ignorant; raw.
comparative form of rude: more rude
superlative form of rude: most rude
Acronym of revision using distal inflow (“a surgical treatment for dialysis-associated steal syndrome”).
Of or relating to one or more rudiments; of the nature of an early stage.
Basic; minimal; with less than, or only the minimum, necessary.
d.x: I have only a rudimentary grasp of chemistry.

d.d: One of the rudimentary (adjective sense 1) mammae of boars.
An acrobatic maneuver involving two and a half twists.
An inspiring competitor, usually an athlete, who perseveres despite tall odds.
